v1_v5.actual: Catalog and KB-body paths both returned their proper citation types. The catalog run preserved one real-provider INVALID_MODEL_RESPONSE and a successful manual retry with five catalog citations. The real-provider KB-body answer cited a permitted Ready Data source; soft-stale serving kept the active version and hard-stale fell back only within the same KB.
v1_v5.expected: Catalog questions use metadata only; body answers use retrieved body evidence. Citations match the served source/version and open to the in-site source.

v1_v5.actual: The identity × server configuration × selected KB matrix used actual retrieval/prompt evidence and generation/embedding counters. Authorized staff used its configured KB; unauthorized identities and spoofed client kb_id/kb_ids were denied; empty, unavailable and mismatched scopes failed before answer generation.
v1_v5.expected: Retrieval is limited to the intersection of caller identity and server configuration. Unauthorized or empty scope is rejected before retrieval/answer generation with zero generation and embedding calls; prompts contain only permitted source IDs.

v1_v5.actual: Live evidence covered catalog/body citations, soft-stale and hard-stale serving, index mismatch, unavailable index and empty scope. Summary-only and no-result edge cases are covered by the focused fixture tests; they are not claimed as separate live-provider runs.
v1_v5.expected: Without usable evidence the request returns a deterministic no-result/error and performs no later answer generation. Any earlier routing/embedding calls are counted separately. Valid stale evidence follows the active serving-version rule.

v1_v5.actual: The four feature-flag combinations were exercised. While off/off, stale-page feedback and assistant POSTs returned 404; refresh hid the entry and yielded no assistant/help/feedback business requests. The actual quota-error→manual-feedback path and assistant-provider format failure are preserved; feedback history remained readable and both flags were restored on.
v1_v5.expected: All four flag combinations behave independently; stale old-page requests are rejected; assistant failure does not block feedback submission or history reads.

v1_v5.actual: Across separate real-browser/API paths, help returned a help citation, catalog returned metadata citations, and KB-body answers cited permitted KB evidence. Auto-classified suggestion text became an editable draft, then persisted after confirmation to isolated PostgreSQL and the existing #461 local inbox. A distinct earlier browser path recorded quota error followed by manual suggestion submit. Desktop and mobile captures are recorded below.
v1_v5.expected: Help, catalog, KB-body and suggestion requests route to the correct source. Suggestions remain editable until confirmed; PostgreSQL and the #461 inbox show the same ID and original text, and saved history survives switch changes.
